title: Smallest Index With Equal Value
statement: You receive an integer array `nums` whose positions are numbered from 0. Look for positions `i` where the remainder of `i` divided by 10 is equal to `nums[i]`, and return the lowest such position. When no position qualifies, return `-1`.
notes:
## Intuition

The question asks for the *smallest* qualifying index, so the natural order to inspect positions is from left to right. The first position that passes the test is automatically the answer, and nothing after it can do better. A brute force that gathers every matching index and takes the minimum gives the same result but keeps scanning needlessly.

## Approach

1. Walk `i` from `0` up to `nums.length - 1`.
2. Compute `i % 10`, the last digit of the index, and compare it with `nums[i]`.
3. On the first match, return `i` immediately.
4. If the loop ends without a match, return `-1`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [0, 1, 2]`. At `i = 0`, `0 % 10 = 0` and `nums[0] = 0`, so they are equal and the function returns `0` straight away. Indices 1 and 2 would also match, but they are never examined because a smaller index already won.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index is checked at most once, and the scan stops at the first match.
- Space: O(1): only the loop counter is kept.

## Pitfalls

- Compare `nums[i]` with `i % 10`, not with `i` itself; from index 10 onward they differ (index 11 matches the value 1).
- Return as soon as a match appears; continuing and overwriting the answer would report the largest index instead.
- Remember the `-1` case when nothing matches, for example `[1, 0]`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `nums` | the input array of digits |
| `i` | the index currently being tested |

narration.1: The function receives the array of digits to scan.
narration.2: Visit the indices in increasing order, so the first hit is the smallest one.
narration.3: Check whether the last digit of the index, i % 10, equals the value stored there.
narration.4: The first index that passes is the answer; return it without looking further.
narration.6: Leaving the loop means every index was tested and none matched.
